chapters.summary: Song of Solomon opens with the bride's longing and her honest self-reflection, portraying both the sweetness of love and its pursuit, along with a humble sense of self-worth.
keyPoints: The bride longs for the bridegroom's love, prizing it above wine, and expresses her deep yearning for him.
The bride describes herself as black but comely, like the tents of Kedar, admitting her outward disadvantage while affirming her inner worth.
The bride seeks closeness with the bridegroom and asks him to lead her, that they may delight in one another in love.
chapters.application: In love, we should be honest about our shortcomings without ever forgetting our own worth. May we, too, seek closeness with the Lord, delight in his presence, and let our daily lives bear witness to love.

chapters.summary: Set against the backdrop of spring, this chapter portrays the loving exchange between the bridegroom and the bride, expressing their mutual belonging and their longing to be near one another.
keyPoints: The bride likens herself to the rose of Sharon, and the bridegroom praises her as a lily among thorns—each delighting in the other.
The bride finds the sweetness of love beneath the apple tree, surrounded by his affection like honey to the taste.
The bridegroom calls the bride to come away with him, that they may keep their tryst of love while spring's flowers are in bloom.
chapters.application: May we treasure our time with the one we love, expressing our affection often in word and deed, creating sweet memories in ordinary days, and letting love bloom like the spring.

chapters.summary: The bride searches for the bridegroom by night and at last finds him within the city; the chapter then describes the splendor of Solomon's wedding litter, a picture of how precious and sacred true love is.
keyPoints: Lovesick in the night, the bride searches everywhere for the bridegroom, showing the depth and persistence of her longing.
Once she finds him, the bride holds him fast and brings him to her mother's house, a picture of love finding its rest and its home.
The magnificence of Solomon's wedding litter is described, its royal splendor mirroring the honor and glory of love itself.
chapters.application: When you feel distant from the Lord in daily life, seek him earnestly as the bride did, hold fast to his promises, and know the security and joy of his presence.

chapters.summary: The bridegroom praises the bride's beauty, pouring out his deep affection for her, and invites her to come away with him, a picture of the goodness and unity that love brings.
keyPoints: The bridegroom uses vivid imagery to praise the bride's eyes, hair, and teeth, highlighting her beauty and purity.
The bridegroom calls the bride "my sister, my spouse," emphasizing their intimacy and his undivided devotion to her.
The bridegroom invites the bride to come with him from Lebanon, a picture of love that rises above circumstance into deeper union.
chapters.application: In marriage or any close relationship, learn to appreciate the other person and offer sincere words of praise, treasuring what makes them unique so that love may grow through respect and devotion.

chapters.summary: This chapter tells of the bride searching for the bridegroom by night, losing him because she delayed in opening the door, then finding him at last in the city, and closing with her praise of his beauty.
keyPoints: Because the bride delays in opening the door, the bridegroom departs, leaving her anxious and searching everywhere for him.
The watchmen of the city strike her as she searches, yet she presses on, showing the persistence of her love.
The bride paints a beautiful portrait of the bridegroom, praising his handsome and altogether lovely appearance.
themes: Loss and Treasuring What We Have
chapters.application: When love is neglected or delayed, seize the moment to express it and respond to it—do not wait until it is lost to feel regret. In faith as well, let us stay watchful and respond promptly to the Lord's call.

chapters.summary: This chapter describes the Shulamite and the bridegroom seeking and praising one another, coming together at last in love, and displaying a devotion that will not waver.
keyPoints: When the daughters of Jerusalem ask where her beloved has gone, the Shulamite declares that he is hers and she is his.
The bridegroom praises the Shulamite as fair as Tirzah and comely as Jerusalem, surpassing sixty queens and eighty concubines.
The Shulamite meets the bridegroom in the garden, and their love, precious as life itself, draws the admiration of the daughters of Jerusalem.
chapters.application: In marriage or a close relationship, let us appreciate one another and remain faithful without wavering. May we, like the lovers in this book, treasure each other, find union in love, and bring glory to God.

chapters.summary: The bridegroom praises the bride's beauty and expresses their deep mutual belonging, then invites her to go out with him to the fields to enjoy the sweetness of love.
keyPoints: The bridegroom praises every part of the bride in beautiful poetry, expressing his heartfelt love for her.
The bride answers the bridegroom's invitation, willing to go with him to the fields and villages to share in the fruit of their love.
Love is as precious as life itself; belonging fully to one another, each is glad to pour out their heart for the other.
chapters.application: In marriage, take time to appreciate what is unique in your spouse, speak words of love, and make it a point to create time alone together, so that love keeps growing warmer even in the midst of ordinary life.

chapters.summary: This chapter portrays the strength and preciousness of love, declaring that love is as strong as death, a flame of the LORD that cannot be quenched.
keyPoints: The bride longs for a closeness with the bridegroom as unguarded as that between siblings, free from the constraints of the world's opinion.
Love is as strong as death, jealousy as cruel as the grave, and many waters cannot quench it.
The bride becomes a keeper of the vineyard, showing that love requires faithfulness and self-giving.
chapters.application: May we treasure the love within marriage, guarding it with faithfulness and devotion, so that it burns on like a flame through the ordinary days of life, bearing witness to the goodness of God's design.
